attacks.claim: Processor deletions run after the DB transaction commits, but the transaction deletes the rows that hold the identifiers those calls need (Apple refresh token, Stripe/Amplitude/Customer.io IDs). The 7-day retry and `purge-failed` ticket cannot work if the identifiers no longer exist. The plan does not say where they are kept, so Apple grants and processor data could be orphaned and Art. 17 missed.
attacks.evidence: "After the DB transaction commits: ... Stripe: detach payment methods ... Sign in with Apple users: `POST /auth/revoke` for their refresh token." ABSENT: where processor IDs and the Apple token persist for retries after purge.

attacks.claim: Only the post-commit processor calls have retry and a dashboard. A failing or stalled nightly `AccountPurgeJob` (transaction timeout, deadlock, job not running) has no alert or maximum time bound. That puts the Art. 17 deadline at risk, and the plan does not say how the nightly job behaves under backlog.
attacks.evidence: "Nightly `AccountPurgeJob` processes accounts whose grace period has ended; each account is one DB transaction" ABSENT: alerting, timeout or backlog behaviour for the DB purge step.

attacks.claim: The plan does not say how the purge job is serialised against a concurrent "Keep my account" or login. Without a status check or lock inside the transaction, an account could be restored while it is being purged.
attacks.evidence: "Keep my account", which restores the account exactly as it was" vs "each account is one DB transaction"; ABSENT: locking or state check.

attacks.claim: Rolling the flag off on iOS hides the in-app deletion entry point that App Store guideline 5.1.1(v) requires. That would recreate the rejection condition for any shipped build.
attacks.evidence: "Rollback: flag off hides the entry points only."

attacks.claim: At purge any still-active Stripe subscription is cancelled. For annual or long-period plans that cuts off paid time, while the plan says refund handling is unchanged.
attacks.evidence: "At purge, any still-active subscription is cancelled. Refunds follow the existing refund policy ... nothing changes there."
